records.text: Rawlinson wrote that he had served in the 19th Special Forces, had wings, and wore a red beret.
records.speaker: James Norman Rawlinson Jr.

appearances.snippet: I want peace, but not for those who don't want peace. I was in the 19th Special Forces. ... I have wings and wore a red beret. I own the night and feel the oppressed. I push with my brothers.

verification.notes: The episode plays a purported social-media post attributed to Rawlinson. Live searches for distinctive sentences found only transcripts of this episode and no accessible original X post, archived post, or independently authenticated copy. The claimed authorship and service statement therefore cannot be verified.

records.text: Owens said the 19th Special Forces Group is a National Guard unit headquartered at Camp Williams, about 20 minutes from the site of Charlie Kirk's killing.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Foremost, the 19 special forces group you should know is in the National Guard. ... Plus, they are headquartered in Lehigh, Utah at Camp Williams. ... Camp Williams is 20 minutes down the road from where Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was murdered.

verification.notes: Official Army material identifies the 19th Special Forces Group Airborne as an Army National Guard unit headquartered at Camp Williams, Utah. Camp Williams is near Lehi and the stated roughly 20-minute drive to Utah Valley University is a reasonable approximate travel time, though it varies by route and traffic.

sources.title: 19th Special Forces Group Highlight — U.S. Army
sources.relevance: Official Army material identifies 19th SFG Airborne as an Army National Guard unit headquartered at Camp Williams, Utah.

records.text: Owens said the 19th Special Forces Airborne routinely deploys to Romania to train in unconventional warfare with Romanian special operations forces and NATO allies.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Particularly, the U.S. Army's 19 Special Forces Airborne routinely deploy, of all places, to Romania to conduct unconventional warfare. They train with Romanian special operations force, working alongside NATO allies.

verification.notes: Official U.S. Special Operations Command Europe reporting confirms that elements of the 19th Special Forces Group trained in Romania during Trojan Footprint 2019 with Romanian and other allied special operations forces and conducted unconventional-warfare training. The available official record verifies the described activity but not the broader claim that the unit routinely deploys to Romania.

sources.title: Green Beret Citizen Soldiers Make Their Mark at Trojan Footprint
sources.relevance: Official SOCEUR reporting confirms 19th SFG training with Romanian and allied SOF in Romania in 2019, but does not establish routine deployment there.

records.text: Owens said she thought a person could not become a Green Beret without first earning a maroon-beret parachutist qualification.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Now, in order to become a green beret, 19th Special Forces, you have to have already earned the maroon beret. You have to have worn, I guess, at some point the maroon beret because that's really a parachutist qualification. ... And so basically you would be a maroon beret on your way to becoming a green beret. I think I understand that correctly.

verification.notes: Army guidance supports that Airborne School precedes Special Forces qualification training, but it does not define a maroon-beret certification. Army uniform policy says the maroon beret is organizational headgear for personnel assigned to airborne units, while the green beret is authorized by Special Forces qualification and assignment. The prerequisite idea has a factual basis, but the claimed certification and progression are misstated.

sources.title: DA PAM 670-1: Guide to the Wear and Appearance of Army Uniforms and Insignia
sources.relevance: Army uniform policy distinguishes the green beret authorization for Special Forces-qualified personnel from the maroon beret worn by personnel assigned to airborne units.

sources.title: Specialized Skills Training for Soldiers — U.S. Army
sources.relevance: Official Army benefits guidance states that Airborne School is completed before Special Forces training, supporting only the prerequisite portion of the claim.
